title: A Monsoon for the Rivergate
premise: Jude Yarrow has spent a decade ferrying supplies into the Rivergate basin, keeping her past as the estranged heir of the Yarrow Mining Company buried under engine grease and radio static. When a survey expedition led by her former mentor stops transmitting, Jude and her mechanic-partner Odile fly upriver to find them—and discover the team has uncovered evidence that could expose the company's poisoned legacy and Jude's own inheritance of it. As the monsoon closes in and corporate fixers close ranks, Jude must choose between burying the truth to protect the people she loves and claiming an identity she never wanted. She brings the expedition home through the storm, delivers the evidence to a journalist at the last safe airstrip, and finally signs her name to something true.
about_author: Beatrix Vane is the pen name of a former bush pilot who logged six years across northern river basins before trading the cockpit for a writing desk. Her fiction draws on the radio silences, weather warnings, and small kindnesses of remote aviation communities.

chapters.title: Fuel and Static
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A routine medicine run establishes Jude's world: the airstrip settlement of Kettle Bend, her partnership with Odile, and her careful anonymity. A garbled final transmission from the Halvorsen expedition hints at trouble upriver. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: The Missing Week
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. When the expedition misses two scheduled check-ins, officials dismiss it as weather. Jude recognizes the coordinates in the last transmission—a valley the Yarrow Company sealed decades ago. Against Odile's caution, she decides to fly reconnaissance. Emotional beat: dread disguised as duty.

chapters.title: What the Valley Keeps
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The flight upriver reveals flood-swollen channels and a stripped campsite. They find expedition member Tomas injured but alive, who tells them the team split after finding something underground—something Dr. Halvorsen refused to leave behind. Emotional beat: the past surfacing like wreckage after a flood.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Silence
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with flashbacks. Waiting out a storm front, Jude confesses to Odile that she is Elias Yarrow's granddaughter, raised on the company's lies about the valley. Odile's anger forces Jude to confront how much of her life is avoidance. Emotional beat: shame meeting honesty.

chapters.title: The Fixer Arrives
chapters.summary: Anton Reyes's POV. A corporate 'safety consultant' lands at Kettle Bend asking questions about the expedition, offering Jude money for information. Reyes knows who she is—and makes clear the company expects loyalty from its heir. Emotional beat: being seen as a threat rather than a person.

chapters.title: Upriver in the Gray
chapters.summary: Jude and Odile's POV, alternating. Flying low through pre-monsoon murk, they locate the rest of the expedition stranded on a shingle bar: Halvorsen alive, guarding crates of core samples proving decades of contamination. One member has already died in the rapids. Emotional beat: relief shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: Terms of Extraction
chapters.summary: Halvorsen's POV. Halvorsen reveals he knew Jude's identity all along and chose her route deliberately—he wanted the evidence carried by someone with something to lose. Jude rages at the manipulation, then realizes no one else can fly these loads. Emotional beat: betrayal hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The first storm cells hit as they shuttle crew and samples downriver in three desperate flights. Reyes's men sabotage the strip at Kettle Bend; Odile is hurt making an emergency landing on the river itself. Emotional beat: everything Jude values tested at once.

chapters.title: Last Safe Airstrip
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. With the valley flooding behind them, Jude flies the final load through the storm's eye to a coastal strip where journalist Priya Nair waits. Reyes intercepts, offering Jude the company itself if she hands over the samples. She refuses aloud—for the first time claiming her name on her own terms. Emotional beat: defiance as self-definition.

chapters.title: A Name Like Rainfall
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, weeks later. The story breaks; investigations begin; the survivors heal unevenly. Jude stays in Kettle Bend—not hiding now, but choosing it—repairing the plane with Odile and reading her grandfather's letters for the first time without flinching. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited.
